title.narrative: UNFPA CSE out of School Phase III

description.narrative:
Norad (establishing donor) supported UNFPA's Global Programme on Out-of-school Comprehencive Sexuality Eeducation (CSE) Phase I during 2018-2021 and Phase II during 2022-2024. In Phase II the program expanded to inclyde 12 countries ( Colombia, Ethiopia, The Philippines, Ghana, Indonesia, Iran, Nicaragua, Nigeria, Malawi, Moldova, Tunisia and Palestine).
UNFPA has applied for Norwegian continued support for Phase III 2025-2028 (november 2024). Norad has decided to support the first year implementation during Q4 in 2025-2026 and will review availiable funding phaseIII. UNFPA submitted a concept note outlining changes.
The programme has three pillars/outcomes that are the same for phase I and II:
Overall goal: To empower and equip adolescents and young people from specific groups left behind with information and skills through out-of-school CSE, so that they can make informed choices about their SRHR and well-being Outcome 1: The Out-of-School Guidance is rolled out at the regional level and adapted to the local contexts in the countries Outcome 2: Participatory, relevant and contextualized programming on out-of-school CSE established and tested. Outcome 3: Documentation and dissemination of strategic information, lessons learned and best practices. Phase III will reinforce the regional scope by adopting a broader implementation approach, directly supporting UNFPA Regional Offices and fostering cross-regional collaboration and knowledge exchange.
UNFPA is transitioning toward a CSE Coordination Mechanism, referred to as the UNFPA Global Initiative for Advancing CSE, which will consolidate Norad’s contribution with other CSE global program
The target groups will be the same as in theprevious phases: Adolescents and young people, returned migrants, refugees, indigenous young people, young people with disabilities, young female sex workers, LGBTQI+ people, young people at risk of HIV, young people living with HIV, and young people in detention.
